clauses.reason: Terminated by Executive Order 12553, signed February 25, 1986 and published at 51 FR 7237 in the Federal Register of March 3, 1986. Its enacting sentence orders that the listed Executive Orders, and "any amendments thereto", are revoked; the text states no delayed effective date and contains no saving clause, so the effective date is the signing date, 1986-02-25 (the printed date, March 3, 1986, is the alternative reading). The table of revoked orders in the held text of Executive Order 12553 lists number 11797 in the number column of the table (the text layer separates the number column from the subject column for this part of the table, so its subject text is not quoted). This order (39 FR 27893, Federal Register of August 2, 1974, signed July 31, 1974) authorizes, under section 901(b) of the Agricultural Act of 1970 (84 Stat. 1383), as amended by section 601 of the Rural Development Act of 1972 (86 Stat. 674; Public Law 92-419), and section 301 of title 3 of the United States Code, the Secretary of Agriculture to exercise the authority vested in the President by section 901(b) in all matters relating to reporting criteria and the preparation and submission of annual reports to the Congress concerning the location of new Federal facilities in rural areas, without approval, ratification or other action by the President; and directs departments and agencies to cooperate with the Secretary in preparing the annual reports required by section 901(b). It is a continuing delegation with no stated end date.

research_rationale:
Identity: the held Federal Register text (39 FR 27893, the issue of August 2, 1974) is Executive Order 11797, dated July 31, 1974; the order is headed Executive Order 11797, Delegating to the Secretary of Agriculture the Function of Submitting an Annual Report to the Congress Concerning the Location of New Federal Facilities in Rural Areas, and is dated July 31, 1974. I read the whole order; the representation is the machine-extracted text layer of the official PDF (OCR for this period), and I did not inspect the page images. End: express revocation by Executive Order 12553 on 1986-02-25. Searches: current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr and later-events:ofr_catalog, each marked complete in the dossier. The U.S. Code search found one editorial note naming this order (under 7 U.S.C. 2204b-1) that recites the revocation by Executive Order 12553; I read the note as a lead and did not rely on it for the ending.

savings.reason: Executive Order 12553, read in full, contains no saving or transition provision: its text is one revoking sentence, a table of the revoked orders, an editorial note and the signature block. The statutory reporting authority is a separate source of law that does not depend on this order. No held claim-grade source shows any command of this order continuing when it was revoked.
